title: Apps and Public Wi-Fi
about: Choose what apps can use, and stay safe on public Wi-Fi.

cards.prompt: Does the app need it for its job?
cards.explanation: Allow what fits the app's job. A torch needs light, not your contacts.
cards.hint: For each one, ask: could the app do its main job without it?
cards.nudge: Think what each app is for. A permission unrelated to that job isn't needed.

cards.sentence: An **app permission** lets an app use your camera, microphone, location or contacts.
For location, pick **"Only while using the app"**, so a closed app can't track you.

cards.prompt: You install a new drawing game.

steps.text: It asks: **"Allow your contacts?"** What do you do?

choices.text: Say no: a drawing game doesn't need them
choices.consequence: Right. The game still works fine without your contacts.

choices.text: Allow it, so the game works
choices.consequence: A drawing game has no reason to see your contacts.
Nice. It only sees your spot while the game is open.
A game doesn't need your location when it's closed.

cards.explanation: Say no to permissions a game doesn't need. For location, pick "Only while using".
cards.hint: Would a drawing game need your contacts, or your location all the time?

cards.prompt: A **microphone dot** shows an app is using the mic.

steps.text: You're not on a call. What do you do?

choices.text: Check which app, and switch its mic off
choices.consequence: Good. You find the app and turn its mic permission off.
The dot means an app is listening right now.
The app still has permission and could listen again later.

cards.explanation: The dot means an app is using the mic. Switch that permission off if it doesn't need it.
cards.hint: The dot means some app is using the mic. Where can you stop it for good?

cards.sentence: **Public Wi-Fi** in cafés and shops is shared, and you can't always be sure it's real.

cards.prompt: Fine on public Wi-Fi, or better on mobile data?
cards.explanation: Everyday browsing is fine. For money or key accounts, use mobile data.
cards.hint: Which ones involve your money or your most important accounts?
cards.nudge: Ask again: does it involve money or an important account?

cards.sentence: A **fake hotspot** is Wi-Fi a stranger names to look like the café's.

cards.prompt: Café Wi-Fi asks for your email password. You type it. What happens?

options.text: Whoever set up that Wi-Fi now has your password
The café checks it, then lets you go online
options.nudge: A real café never needs your email password. This could be a fake hotspot.

options.text: Nothing: Wi-Fi pages can't keep what you type
options.nudge: A sign-in page sends what you type to whoever made it.

options.text: Your email app spots the wrong page and blocks it
options.nudge: Your email app never sees this page. You're the only check.

cards.explanation: Anyone can name Wi-Fi after the café and ask for passwords. Real café Wi-Fi never needs your email password: ask staff for its name.
cards.hint: Who made the sign-in page, and who gets what you type into it?

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- Give apps only the **permissions** they need; pick **"Only while using"** for location.
- On **public Wi-Fi**, check the name, and bank on **mobile data**.
- **Try this:** switch one app's location to "Only while using".

**Next:** how to tell when an account has been taken over.
